checks.name: Programme metadata groups the three scheduled sessions into one real assignment
Versioned assigned sessions load without fake purchases or history
Second patient starts with an honest empty plan
Programme metadata is not visible to another patient
Missing account session is denied
Lost-response start retry returns the same persisted attempt
Only one open attempt exists for a scheduled session
Sibling patient cannot read or change the attempt
Direct table read enforces row-level isolation
Empty attempt cannot be marked complete
Set save retries are idempotent
Reusing a command ID with changed actuals is rejected
Only the acknowledged actual set is recorded
Pause stores elapsed time and stops the running clock
Stale session revision is rejected
Session, set, identity and pause survive database close and reopen
Completion retry does not create a duplicate record
Completed actuals cannot be silently rewritten
A genuine repeat has a separate attempt and preserves old history
Assigned practitioner can read but cannot overwrite patient actuals
Practitioner mutation of patient actuals is denied
Patient cannot alter published programme versions directly
Check-in sharing requires explicit acknowledgement
Shared check-in persists only within its relationship
Public catalogue exposes only public fields
Availability reveals no patient identity or private calendar fields
Concurrent local requests for the last time produce one reservation
Reservation retry returns the original booking
Overlapping appointment at a different start time is rejected by PostgreSQL
Another patient cannot read or cancel the reservation
Appointment survives database restart
Cancellation retains history and releases the allocated time
Multiple assignments of one version remain two independent programmes
Programme library grouping does not alter saved session history
Published metadata remains protected by row-level permissions
Server session revocation prevents later data access

engine: PGlite local PostgreSQL; synthetic provider-shaped auth, not Supabase Auth
concurrency: Concurrent API dispatches are serialized by the single local database process; multi-connection production stress remains untested
